You are a debugging assistant. You have access to the source code of the system under test (SUT), the failing test case (signature + snippet), the current issue report describing the failure.

Your task is to provide a step-by-step explanation of how the bug occurred using all available evidence:
– the failing test (signature + snippet),
– the current bug report,
– and code snippets of methods from the SUT.

Some identifiers in the current bug report may be anonymized with placeholders (e.g., C#.M#). If the same token (e.g., C1) appears multiple times, it consistently refers to the same class (C) or method (M) throughout the report. These tokens are not complete qualified names. Always confirm actual identifiers by inspecting the source code using get_code_snippet.

You will be given 9 opportunities to interact with functions to gather information for the debugging. An example diagnosis would look like follows.

Title: Diagnosis
Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

messages.content: " * Green implementation of regionMatches. * * @param cs * the CharSequence to be processed * @param ignoreCase * whether or not to be case insensitive * @param thisStart * the index to start on the cs CharSequence * @param substring * the CharSequence to be looked for * @param start * the index to start on the substring CharSequence * @param length * character length of the region * @return whether the region matched "

Title: Diagnosis
Details: The failing test exercises StringUtils.equals(CharSequence, CharSequence) with StringBuilder inputs, including a case where the two sequences have different lengths: "abc" vs "abcd". Inspecting the implementation:

- StringUtils.equals(CharSequence, CharSequence) (lines 71–81) handles nulls and short-circuits for String instances, but for general CharSequence it calls:
  CharSequenceUtils.regionMatches(cs1, false, 0, cs2, 0, Math.max(cs1.length(), cs2.length()))
  i.e., it asks to compare a region whose length is the maximum of the two sequence lengths.

- CharSequenceUtils.regionMatches(CharSequence, boolean, int, CharSequence, int, int) (lines 49–78) implements a character-by-character loop for the specified length, but it does not perform any bounds checking before accessing characters. It assumes the caller provides a valid region length, and simply does:
  while (tmpLen-- > 0) {
      char c1 = cs.charAt(index1++);
      char c2 = substring.charAt(index2++);
      ...
  }

Given the test case with cs1 = new StringBuilder("abc") (length 3) and cs2 = new StringBuilder("abcd") (length 4), equals computes length = Math.max(3, 4) = 4 and calls regionMatches with length 4. The loop then tries to read cs1.charAt(3) on the fourth iteration, which throws a StringIndexOutOfBoundsException because valid indices are 0–2.

Thus:
- The test expects equals("abc", "abcd") to return false, but the current code throws due to reading past the end of the shorter sequence.
- The root cause is twofold:
  1) StringUtils.equals uses Math.max(cs1.length(), cs2.length()) as the compared region length, which can exceed the bounds of the shorter sequence.
  2) CharSequenceUtils.regionMatches does not guard against out-of-bounds access (unlike String.regionMatches, which returns false when the requested region exceeds bounds).

Either correcting equals to compare only when lengths are equal (or to pass the shorter length and additionally check lengths) or making regionMatches mimic String.regionMatches by returning false when the requested region exceeds the bounds would prevent the exception and satisfy the test expectation.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).

StringUtils.equals(CharSequence, CharSequence)
CharSequenceUtils.regionMatches(CharSequence, boolean, int, CharSequence, int, int)
